brief: The AI selloff is shifting into a broader positioning washout. Tech CDS spreads are widening alongside falling tech stocks, a reversal from the prior pattern where CDS spikes coincided with a rising Nasdaq 100. Hedge funds have been net sellers of global AI stocks for five sessions, cutting net allocation to 26.1% from a June peak of 31.7%, and the aggregate long/short ratio has fallen from 4.34 to 3.27 (7th percentile over the past year), which points to de-grossing rather than a simple net-exposure cut. Foreign investors have sold $11.6bn of Korean tech over eight sessions (SK Hynix 15 straight days, Samsung five), though domestic buyers are absorbing some of that supply. Memory stocks are falling even as DDR5 spot prices keep rising and Samsung and SK Hynix trade near 1.2x and 0.9x book, implying equities are already pricing a downturn by 2028 that has not shown up in physical pricing yet. NDX forward P/E is back near 21x, a level one Goldman strategist reads as a possible supportive setup into earnings. Separately, Indian IT has rallied as the anti-AI rotation beneficiary, and Brazilian equity implied volatility has spiked ahead of the election even as the ETF itself is flat.
